Block-diagonal sensitivity of the directed layer

Source: R/dag_layer.R
mc_dag_sensitivity.Rd

Assembles the model-based Pearson sensitivity \(\mathbf J_n\) of the directed layer from its closed form. The empirical sandwich and two-stage covariance functions use the observed Hessian of the working criterion instead, since a sparse directed acyclic graph (DAG) can omit second-moment structure. On the accumulated scale, with \(P_j\) the parents of response \(j\) and \(\boldsymbol\gamma_j\) their coefficients, $$\mathbf J_{n,\boldsymbol\gamma_j\boldsymbol\gamma_j}= \frac{n}{\delta_j}\boldsymbol\Sigma_{b,P_jP_j},\qquad J_{n,\delta_j\delta_j}=\frac{n}{2\delta_j^2},$$ and every other block vanishes: between the coefficients of distinct responses, between coefficients and innovation variances, and between innovation variances of distinct responses. The generic assembly used by the fitting engine forms \(P^2\) traces of \(R \times R\) products; this form costs one block per node.

Usage

mc_dag_sensitivity(Sigma_b, delta, n, R, edges = NULL)

Arguments

Sigma_b

the fitted \(R \times R\) covariance of the layer.

delta

the \(R\) innovation variances.

n

number of experimental units.

R

a single positive integer, the number of responses.

edges

optional integer matrix with columns \((i, j)\), \(i < j\), the directed edges \(i \to j\). If NULL, the complete DAG on the natural ordering \(1 < 2 < \dots < R\) is used. Each edge must occur exactly once; duplicated rows, including reversed duplicates, are rejected because they do not define distinct structural coordinates. A row given as \((j, i)\) with \(j > i\) is read as the same edge \(i \to j\): the direction always follows the natural order of the responses. The rows are sorted lexicographically before use, and gamma is read in that sorted order, not in the order the rows were supplied. Sort the matrix yourself, or read the order back from the edges component of the result, whenever the correspondence matters.

Value

The \((|E| + R) \times (|E| + R)\) symmetric, block-diagonal sensitivity in the parameter order c(gamma, delta), where \(|E|\) is the number of edges and the gamma entries follow the sorted order of the edges (see edges in mc_build_T_matrix).

See also

mc_dag_closed_root

Other directed layer: mc_build_D_matrix(), mc_build_T_matrix(), mc_cholesky_derivatives(), mc_cholesky_to_covariance(), mc_cholesky_to_precision(), mc_dag_closed_root(), mc_dag_coefficients(), mc_dag_unit_diagonal()

Examples

cc <- mc_cholesky_to_covariance(c(0.7, 0.3, 0.5), c(1, 0.64, 0.49), R = 3)
J <- mc_dag_sensitivity(cc$Sigma_b, c(1, 0.64, 0.49), n = 100, R = 3)
round(J, 6)
